answersToBriefQuestions.a_endpoints_that_trigger_email: None. The module exposes zero application endpoints (0 @RestController/@Controller/@RequestMapping - see endpointGroups[]), so nothing is authenticated and nothing is un-authenticated either. The only code path that sends mail is the scheduler: BirthdayListenerService.java:16-17 -> :31 -> MailService.java:60. Service-level authentication does not exist at all: spring-boot-starter-security and spring-security-oauth2-resource-server are absent from notification-service/pom.xml:16-67, so the only HTTP that does answer - /actuator/** (exposed "*", notification-service.yml:14-17) and /image/imageQRCode.png - is unauthenticated at the service level. Its only real protection is accidental: server.port: 0 gives no stable port and gateway-service.yml:38-51 has no route to it.
answersToBriefQuestions.b_mail_property_names: config-service/src/main/resources/config/notification-service.yml, block spring.mail at lines 36-56. NAMES present: spring.mail.host (37 - value is the hostname smtp.gmail.com, cited as a hostname, not a credential), spring.mail.port (38 = 587), spring.mail.username (39), spring.mail.password (40), spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.auth (46 = true), spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.starttls.enable (51-52 = true). Lines 39-40 are PLAINTEXT LITERALS - no ${...} indirection, no default, no secret-store reference; they are committed credentials and their values are intentionally not reproduced here in any form, including masked or truncated. The auth/starttls booleans are literals too but are not secrets. ABSENT: any mail.enabled-style flag (no kill switch - mail cannot be stopped without a code change), spring.mail.default-encoding, spring.mail.protocol, spring.mail.from / from-address; COMMENTED OUT: smtp.connectiontimeout|timeout|writetimeout (47-49), starttls.required (53), socketFactory.* for SSL/465 (55-56). Consequence of the commented timeout block: javaMailSender.send() at MailService.java:28 and :60 can block on the JavaMail default read timeout and stall the only scheduler thread.
answersToBriefQuestions.c_rate_limit_or_dedupe: None. No RateLimit / @Async / @Retryable / RetryTemplate / spring-retry / cache dependency in notification-service/pom.xml, and no in-memory or persisted "already sent" marker. The sole throttle is @Scheduled(fixedDelay = DateUtils.MILLIS_PER_DAY) at BirthdayListenerService.java:16 - a delay, not a rate limit and not an idempotency guard - so a restart before the delay elapses re-sends the same mail to the same hard-coded recipients (MailService.java:23 -> 2 addresses, :39 -> 1 address), with no configurable burst target.

No Feign client, no RestTemplate, no WebClient, no DiscoveryClient lookup targets it; gateway-service.yml:38-51 routes only to auth-service, user-service and person-service; no Kafka topic links anything (spring-kafka in 0 poms). The would-be caller, user-service, owns its own disabled pair instead - user-service/src/main/java/pro/algotrade/userservice/service/NotificationService.java:3 and .../service/impl/MailServiceImpl.java:10-17, whose KafkaTemplate body is commented out. recommendations: Credentials (P0, already tracked in .opencode/project_init.md): replace the two literals at notification-service.yml:39-40 with ${SMTP_USERNAME}/${SMTP_PASSWORD}, rotate, purge git history. While that file is open, add a mail.enabled-style flag - today outbound mail cannot be stopped without deleting code.

Delete or wire the dead path sendEmail() (:20-29, zero callers); either drop spring-boot-starter-test or add the first test - MailService is trivially testable with a mocked JavaMailSender (or GreenMail), no new dependency for the mock.

Small hardening: fix NotificaServicetionApplication (:9, safe rename) and either scope commons-lang3 to compile (pom.xml:37) or inline the 86 400 000 ms constant, so the build stops depending on a constant-inlining accident.
